title: Mechanical Engineer
description: Van net afgestudeerd tot ervaren engineer: bouw met ons mee aan techniek die je niet iedere dag tegenkomt. Royal SMIT groeit. Daarom breiden we ons Engineering-team in Nijmegen flink uit en zoeken we meerdere Mechanical Engineers. Of je nu aan het begin van je carrière staat, al een paar jaar ervaring hebt of toe bent aan een volgende stap als ervaren engineer: bij ons krijg je de ruimte om op jouw niveau in te stappen én verder te groeien. Je werkt aan indrukwekkende vermogenstransformatoren voor klanten over de hele wereld. En omdat Engineering en Productie bij ons op dezelfde locatie zitten, blijft het niet bij een ontwerp op je beeldscherm. Wat jij ontwerpt, zie je hier daadwerkelijk gebouwd worden. Wat ga je doen? Als Mechanical Engineer werk je aan het mechanische buitenwerk van onze vermogenstransformatoren. Denk aan de tank, koeling, expansievaten, ventilatoren, pompen en het complete oliecircuit. Geen project is hetzelfde. Van aardbevingsbestendigheid en transport tot koeling, geluid en extreme weersomstandigheden: jij vertaalt technische eisen naar slimme, veilige én maakbare oplossingen. Je houdt je onder andere bezig met: Ontwerpen en construeren in 3D CAD; Uitvoeren en beoordelen van technische berekeningen; Ontwerpen toetsen op kwaliteit, veiligheid, maakbaarheid en kosten; Samenwerken met collega’s binnen Engineering en Operations; Oplossen van technische vraagstukken binnen projecten; Bijdragen aan innovatie en verbetering van onze ontwerpen. Hoe snel je verantwoordelijkheid krijgt, hangt af van jouw ervaring en ontwikkeling. Iedere engineer start bij ons met een inwerktraject waarin je ons unieke product, onze processen en onze manier van werken leert kennen. Als starter krijg je daarbij intensieve begeleiding van ervaren collega’s. Breng je al relevante ervaring mee, dan zul je het inwerktraject op onderdelen sneller doorlopen en eerder zelfstandig technische vraagstukken en projecten oppakken. Naarmate je groeit in je rol, krijg je steeds meer verantwoordelijkheid en ruimte om complexere uitdagingen aan te pakken. Wat breng je mee? We zoeken vooral engineers die enthousiast worden van techniek en graag willen blijven leren. Je hebt: Je hebt een afgeronde technische opleiding op mbo-, hbo- of wo-niveau, waarbij relevante werkervaring binnen engineering voor ons minstens zo belangrijk is als je opleidingsniveau Kennis van of ervaring met 3D CAD en mechanisch construeren; Affiniteit met constructieleer en technische berekeningen; Oog voor kwaliteit, veiligheid en maakbaarheid; Een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal. title: Mechanical Engineer (m/f/d)
description: Job Description ATMOS Works is seeking a Mechanical Engineer (m/f/d) with strong expertise in CAD-based development, mechanical design, and hands-on experience in building aerospace-grade hardware. Key responsabilities You will develop and refine mechanical designs from concept through production, ensuring space-qualification requirements are met. You will create detailed 3D CAD models and technical drawings, preferably in SolidWorks, for manufacturing and assembly processes. You will lead the mechanical design, analysis, and optimization of launcher structures, mechanisms, and interfaces for performance, durability, and mass efficiency. You will define materials, components, and manufacturing methods compliant with aerospace standards and environmental constraints. You will manage and support the end-to-end manufacturing process, including prototype builds, assembly, integration, and test campaigns. You will conduct and document mechanical, structural, and environmental testing, including vibration, thermal cycling, and fit checks. You will collaborate closely with internal teams, including systems, avionics, and propulsion, to ensure seamless integration of mechanical subsystems. You will interface with suppliers and partners to clarify technical specifications and ensure component quality and compliance. You will continuously improve existing designs to enhance performance, reliability, manufacturability, and cost efficiency. You will ensure full traceability, documentation, and compliance with safety, aerospace, and certification requirements. Requirements Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. Professional experience in mechanical design through internships, working student roles, university projects, or an entry-level engineering position. Good knowledge of 3D CAD modelling and technical drawing; experience with SolidWorks is a strong plus. Initial hands-on experience with mechanical assembly, prototype development, or testing is an advantage. Solid understanding of mechanical structures, materials, and manufacturing processes. Interest in designing hardware for demanding environments, including vibration, thermal loads, and other challenging operating conditions. Ability to understand technical requirements and translate them into practical and robust mechanical designs. Strong written and spoken German; English is a strong plus. Structured and proactive way of working, with strong problem-solving skills and a hands-on mindset. **Please note that we can only consider applicants who are nationals of an EU member state .** Company description ATMOS Works is a dedicated business unit of ATMOS Space Cargo, based in Kraków, Poland, and established to serve European government and defence customers. It develops and operates dual-use orbital capabilities, including the secure, sovereign return of sensitive hardware and data, in-orbit demonstration and validation (IOD/IOV), and advanced space systems. ATMOS was founded as a European company built on the values of freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law, and human rights. We are committed to protect these values by making our technology available to others who share the same values, strengthening infrastructure and innovation for prosperity on Earth.Our team is multinational and diverse, with offices in Lichtenau and Strasbourg. We work in a collegial, hands-on culture where people support each other, take ownership, and keep learning every day. Motivation for the mission comes first — building spacecraft is not a nine-to-five pursuit. We align the mission, the team, and the individual in mutual dependence. This principle shapes our work environment where exceptional people, as committed as they are competent, can grow and contribute to a mission that matters.

Sa mission : contribuer durablement à un monde plus sûr, où le transport aérien devient toujours plus respectueux de l'environnement, plus confortable et plus accessible. Implanté sur tous les continents, le Groupe emploie 100 000 collaborateurs pour un chiffre d'affaires de 27,3 milliards d'euros en 2024, et occupe, seul ou en partenariat, des positions de premier plan mondial ou européen sur ses marchés. Safran est la 2ème entreprise du secteur aéronautique et défense du classement « World's Best Companies 2024 » du magazine TIME. Safran Aerosystems est l'un des leaders mondiaux des systèmes aéronautiques dédiés à la sécurité des avions et hélicoptères ainsi qu'à la gestion des fluides et du carburant. La société est un acteur clé dans le domaine de la sécurité des vols (oxygène, évacuation, flottabilités) et participe à la décarbonation de l'aviation grâce aux carburants alternatifs durables et aux nouvelles architectures moteurs. Elle compte 5200 collaborateurs répartis dans 7 pays. Parce que nous sommes persuadés que chaque talent compte, nous valorisons et encourageons les candidatures de personnes en situation de handicap pour nos opportunités d'emploi Vous souhaitez intégrer un grand Groupe aéronautique leader sur ses marchés avec de grands défis à relever ? La Division Aerosafety (DASY) développe une large gamme de systèmes gonflables (toboggans d'évacuation, flottabilités de secours d'hélicoptères, radeaux et gilets de sauvetage) pour aéronefs commerciaux et militaires ainsi que des systèmes oxygène pour les pilotes et passagers. Vous intégrerez la Business Unit Oxygen Systems, qui conçoit des systèmes et équipements oxygène destinés à assurer la sécurité des équipages et des passagers à bord des avions civils et militaires et des hélicoptères. En tant qu'Ingénieur-e Produit, vous serez en charge de concevoir, de justifier et de maintenir la définition des équipements Oxygène développés pour l'aviation civile et militaire (masques à oxygène pour pilotes, systèmes de distribution et de régulation...). Vous serez en charge des étapes clés du développement de nouveaux produits et d'évolutions de systèmes existants. Pour se faire, vous mènerez les activités suivantes : - Développer des produits et sous-ensembles respectant les exigences Client, en établissant les spécifications en collaboration avec les Ingénieur-es Systèmes. - Construire la définition de l'équipement et sa justification en : - élaborant la définition de l'équipement avec l'aide des concepteurs ou conceptrices de l'équipe, tout en veillant à la pertinence technico-économique des solutions, - spécifiant des calculs et des simulations numériques auprès des Ingénieur-es Simulations, - spécifiant les programmes d'essais de mise au point, de développement et de qualification auprès du Laboratoire d'essais, et en validant les résultats. - Piloter l'ensemble des travaux de développement et de qualification de l'équipement. Ce poste pourrait être évolutif vers un rôle de manager hiérarchique. Vous savez gérer des projets de développement Produit et déployer une approche basée sur la gestion du risque, des coûts et du respect des délais ? Vous serez amené-e, lors de faits techniques, à appliquer les méthodes d'expertise et de résolution de problèmes. Vous avez un diplôme Bac+5 et possédez une forte expérience (supérieure à 8 ans) dans le développement d'équipements mécaniques ou pneumatiques pour l'éronautique ? Les compétences techniques recherchées : - Expériences réalisées dans le développement d'équipements aéronautiques civils (DO-160) - Bonnes compétences en mécanique et matériaux (résistance, lois de comportement, tenue en statique et en fatigue, lecture de plan, chaîne de cote...), ainsi qu'en pneumatique. - Maîtrise des méthodes d'analyses fonctionnelles et de Fiabilité et Sécurité de Fonctionnement (AMDEC, évènements redoutés, arbres de défaillance...). - Des connaissances en CAO (Catia v5), en simulations numériques structure, vous seront nécessaires pour échanger avec les membres de l'équipe. Le savoir-être recherché : - Rigueur, sérieux et orientation satisfaction Client, - Esprit d'équipe et excellentes qualités relationnelles, - Autonomie, polyvalence, proactivité et transparence. - Appétence pour le management d'équipe Vous recherchez un nouveau challenge pour « booster » votre carrière ? Alors ce poste est fait pour vous ! Embarquez dans une aventure à taille humaine ! - Primes d'intéressement et de participation, abondement sur le Plan Epargne Salariale - Remboursement du titre de transport à hauteur de 75 % - CSE avec réductions sur la billetterie, chèques vacances, chèques cadeaux, participation aux activités sportives et culturelles… - Programme de cooptation

title: Marie Curie PhD vacancy (DC8) for PhD research titled "Additive manufacturing of ceramics with complex surfaces for small-scale turbomachinery"
description: The PhD research will be carried out in the Advanced Ceramics and Powder Metallurgy team at the Department of Materials Engineering of KU Leuven. KU Leuven (University of Leuven) has been a center of learning for nearly six centuries since 1425, making it one of the oldest and most renowned universities in Europe. Today, it is Belgium’s highest ranked university (QS 2025 : 60), ranked among the top 4% universities in the world and consistently ranked in the top 10 most innovative universities in Europe. The university caters to over 60,000 students from more than 140 countries. KU Leuven's three doctoral schools provide internationally oriented PhD tracks for more than 4,000 doctoral students. KU Leuven and affiliated knowledge institutes provide fertile ground for innovation and high-tech entrepreneurship in the Leuven region. This favorable climate for knowledge-driven innovation makes the Leuven region an attractive location for many high-tech companies. KU Leuven website: https://www.kuleuven.be/english/kuleuven/ Project KU Leuven seeks a highly motivated PhD candidate for a fully funded, four-year international doctoral position within the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN) project TURBO-IMPACT (TURBOmachinery Innovative Manufacturing, Processing, Analysis, Characterization, and Topology ; Website: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311350). The TurboImpact project, funded by Horizon Europe – MSCA-DN, tackles challenges in designing, optimizing, selecting materials, and manufacturing small-scale turbomachinery for applications in heat pumps, fuel cells, organic Rankine cycles, or gas turbines. This project develops robust system and component design methods, an integrated manufacturing platform, and multi-material joining techniques to efficiently produce small-scale turbomachinery. In this EU project, this PhD researcher (DC8) will focus on the complete indirect DLP/SLA additive manufacturing route for silicon nitride turbomachinery components. This involves the development of a UV-curable Si3N4 slurry, optimization of DLP/SLA printing strategies for reference parts and complex components such as impellers, and the post-printing debinding and sintering process to obtain fully dense complex near-net-shaped ceramic components. The AM parts will be microstructurally, mechanically and geometrically characterized. Simple geometries will be used for the evaluation of joining and machining performances, whereas the complex near-net-shaped components will be applied in turbomachinery. The Doctoral Candidate Will Develop a UV-curable Si3N4 slurry and optimize DLP/SLA printing strategies for reference parts and complex components Realize post-printing debinding and sintering processes to obtain fully dense complex near-net-shaped ceramic components Elucidate the processing – microstructure – mechanical properties – geometrical accuracy correlations. The project includes potential international secondments at EPFL (Switzerland), Admatec Additive Solutions (The Netherlands) and IFW (Germany). The researcher is supervised by Prof. Jozef Vleugels (https://www.kuleuven.be/wieiswie/nl/person/00006337), head of the Functional Materials Division (FUNMAT) and coordinator of the Advanced Ceramics and Powder Metallurgy research group at the Department of Materials Engineering. The research group has a long track record (>35 years) on the powder metallurgical development, processing and characterisaton of ceramics, cermets, metcers and metals. More information on the website (https://www.mtm.kuleuven.be/english/research/siem/ACPM) Profile I have a two-year master degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, or an equivalent master degree. I am proficient in written and spoken English. During my courses, master thesis or prior professional activities, I have gathered basic experience on the processing of ceramics, additive manufacturing, microstructural and mechanical characterization or I have a profound interest in these topics. I demonstrate a strong sense of initiative and responsibility, while also being an effective and collaborative team player. I am very motivated and obtained good grades (minimum distinction level) I feel comfortable to work as a team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and be inspired by my colleagues. Special requirements: In accordance with the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network regulations: Applicants must comply with the MSCA Mobility Rule. At the time of recruitment, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the hiring Country for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding recruitment. Applicants must be doctoral candidates (i.e., not already hold a doctoral degree) and be eligible under the MSCA Doctoral Network rules at the time of recruitment Short stays such as holidays, compulsory national service, or time spent as part of a refugee procedure are not considered. Applicants must have a two-year master's degree in Materials Engineering, Materials Science, or an equivalent master degree , or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. description: This proposed PhD research will be carried out in the Additive Manufacturing (AM) team at the Department of Mechanical Engineering from KU Leuven. KU Leuven (University of Leuven) has been a center of learning for nearly six centuries since 1425, making it one of the oldest and most renowned universities in Europe. Today, it is Belgium’s highest ranked university (QS 2025 : 60), ranked among the top 4% universities in the world and consistently ranked in the top 10 most innovative universities in Europe. In that large EU project, This PhD researcher (DC7) will work at KU Leuven and focus on increasing the fundamental understanding of multi-metal Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) additive manufacturing for small-scale turbomachinery. title: PhD positions in Structural Health Monitoring of Welded Thermoplastic Composite Assemblies
description: Job Description Thermoplastic composites are widely regarded as promising materials for the next generation of commercial aircraft, combining excellent mechanical performance with low weight. In addition, their melt-processable matrix enables automated, high-rate manufacturing of components that can subsequently be assembled into complex aerostructures using welding. This provides significant opportunities for more efficient and cost-effective aircraft manufacturing. However, welded composite assemblies are challenging to inspect using conventional non-destructive inspection techniques. As a result, larger safety margins are often required in structural design, leading to heavier structures, while maintenance intervals may be more conservative than necessary. Developing reliable methods to continuously assess the structural condition therefore enable both lighter designs and more efficient maintenance strategies. To address this challenge, the project aims to develop structural health monitoring technologies based on a digital twin . The digital twin will combine information from the physical structure with models and monitoring data to assess its current structural state and predict its remaining lifetime. This will enable the condition of welded structures to be monitored throughout their service life, allowing maintenance to be planned when it is actually needed rather than according to predetermined intervals. Ultimately, this approach aims to contribute to lighter, safer, and more sustainable aircraft structures . The PhD positions Experimental characterization and digital twin development A key challenge in developing a reliable digital twin is accurately characterizing the static and fatigue behaviour of welded thermoplastic composite joints. Since there are currently no well-established standards for fatigue testing of these joints, the project will involve developing experimental methods to reliably characterize their mechanical performance and damage evolution. The experimental results will be used to develop constitutive models for the welded interface. In particular, these models should describe progressive interfacial damage development as a function of fatigue loading. The models will be implemented and validated in commercial finite element (FE) software. The resulting FE model will define the digital twin of the welded structure and provide the basis for the second PhD project, which will use the digital twin together with monitoring data to develop prognostic structural health monitoring strategies. In this project you will: Perform experimental characterization of the static and fatigue performance of welded thermoplastic composite structures. Develop constitutive models that accurately describe the performance of the welded interface. Implement the developed models in commercial FE simulation software for the development of a digital twin and validate their accuracy against experiments. We are looking for a colleague who has experience in mechanical experimentation of the fatigue behavior of composite materials and/or polymers, and is able to develop and implement constitutive models in FE software. Development of a Structural Health Monitoring system The ability to estimate the current state of the welded thermoplastic composite joint and the development of this state over time, is of decisive importance for lifetime performance modelling. The key challenges are the robust integration of a sensor system in the structure and the analysis of measured signals, which are typically strongly affected by environmental and operational conditions. This project aims to tackle these challenges by using piezo-electric and/or optical fiber based sensor system, combined with physics informed data analysis method, exploiting the digital twin model developed by the first PhD project. In this project you will: Implement an effective sensor integration method for welded thermoplastic composite structures, using piezo-electric sensors, fiber optical sensor, or a combination of both. Perform dynamic experiments of pristine and (gradually) damaged structures to collect data for the state estimation methods. Develop signal processing methods to estimate, enriched by physics-based information, the current state of the welded structure and its development under fatigue loading. We are looking for a colleague who has experience in sensor integration and dynamic experimentation, knowledge of piezo-electric or optical fiber based measurements, and proficiency in signal processing methods enriched with physics-based information. Your profile You are a highly motivated researcher who is driven by curiosity and has: A Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or equivalent. Good team-working abilities and a positive can-do mentality. Strong reporting and communication skills Proficiency in English, both spoken and written (we require a TOEFL > 90 or IELTS > 6.5 score). Further, the position on fatigue characterization and mechanical modelling requires: Experimental skills in the mechanical characterization of fiber reinforced composites or polymers; experience with fatigue testing is desired. Theoretical knowledge and skills in the modelling of (failure) of fiber reinforced composites. Experience with the finite element method and programming experience in scripting languages like Python or Matlab. The position on structural health monitoring requires: Experimental and theoretical skills in dynamics and experiences with piezo-electric and/or fiber optic sensors. Experience with signal processing methods of data, enriched with physics-based information. Our offer We offer a full-time 4-year Ph.D. position with a qualifier in the first year; excellent mentorship in a stimulating research environment with excellent facilities; and a personal development program within the Twente Graduate School. description: Travaillant au sein de l’équipe « Technology » de l’ingénierie Produit, l’ingénieur(e) calcul en intégrité mécanique réalise des analyses statiques, dynamiques et thermomécaniques sur les composants et assemblages des produits nucléaires. Ces produits incluent notamment la turbine à vapeur, l’alternateur, les pompes, les échangeurs de chaleur et leurs systèmes auxiliaires. Le rôle comprend également la contribution au développement et à l’amélioration des méthodes et outils dédiés aux analyses d’intégrité mécanique, afin de garantir la fiabilité et la performance des équipements. Les missions clés : Réaliser des analyses d’intégrité mécanique par la méthode des éléments finis sur des composants, conformément aux critères de dimensionnement et aux règles et instructions internes. Modéliser des structures complexes à l’aide du logiciel de maillage HyperMesh et effectuer des simulations par éléments finis sous ANSYS. Personnaliser les modèles, automatiser les cas de charge et effectuer des post-traitements avancés à l’aide du langage APDL (Ansys Parametric Design Language). Réaliser des analyses statiques et dynamiques (modales, sismiques, harmoniques, transitoires), ainsi que des études de durée de vie (fatigue, nocivité, propagation de fissures). Effectuer des calculs mécaniques linéaires et non linéaires (non-linéarités de contact, de comportement matériau et de géométrie). Intégrer les exigences des codes (CODAP, EN 13445, ASME, RCC-M) dans les études de dimensionnement des appareils à pression. Prendre en charge les analyses mécaniques dans le cadre de l’exécution des projets et/ou du développement produit. Coordination technique entre les équipes calculs MI et les équipes design et de management de projet. Représente l’activité calcul MI au sein de revues d’avancement projet Proposer, planifier et exécuter les activités de projet en lien avec le responsable de l’équipe Intégrité Mécanique, incluant la mise en œuvre de méthodes et d’outils de calcul adaptés. Rédiger les rapports d’analyse d’intégrité mécanique conformément aux exigences qualité et aux plannings définis. Vérifier les calculs et analyses réalisés par d’autres membres de l’équipe. Assurer le suivi technique des activités sous-traitées. Contribuer au développement et à l’harmonisation des outils, processus de calcul et à la capitalisation du savoir-faire. Promouvoir le savoir-faire et l’image du département. Agir conformément aux valeurs et au code d’éthique de l’entreprise. Respecter les règles et instructions EHS propres à l’entreprise. Diplôme d’ingénieur ou doctorat dans le domaine du calcul d’intégrité mécanique. Minimum 10 ans d’expérience dans le domaine du calcul mécanique de structures par éléments finis. title: Test Tooling Engineer
description: Do you want to change how the world creates? At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before. In this role you will help building and shipping PreForm , own PreForm's quality and performance signal - make quality automated, measurable, and enforced at the PR gate. We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us. The Job: Performance regression detection. Per-PR and nightly measurement of the defined KPIs (startup, upload, print generation, crash rate) in CI, with alerting on regression. This is the enforcement mechanism for the PreForm performance initiative. Systemtest re-architecture on the PreForm Local API. Rebuild the systemtest layer to drive end-to-end scenarios headlessly through PreForm Server, in alignment with the API team. Customer-file corpus testing. Build and own a pipeline that runs large batches of real customer models through slicing and support generation and diffs results against baselines - catching regressions on the geometry customers actually print, at a scale manual testing cannot reach. Crash intelligence. Own Sentry triage, trending, and root-cause attribution; build crash-reproduction harnesses so engineers fix rather than investigate. Test infrastructure stewardship. Print regression baselines, CI flake, test runtimes, golden-file management - owned as a product instead of taxing feature engineers. You: C++ proficiency. Able to write integration and system tests against PreForm internals and understand what they exercise (mesh operations, print file generation, slicing output). Not necessarily a geometry expert; not afraid of the codebase. Python for tooling and harnesses. Corpus pipelines, API-driven test drivers, result diffing and reporting. CI and automation depth. Jenkins, test parallelization, flake management, baseline/golden-file testing strategies. Observability instinct. Sentry, Amplitude, crash and performance dashboards. Treats 'is this release healthy' as a data question. Desktop application testing experience (strong plus). GUI automation on Windows/macOS (Squish or Qt Test-based harnesses) Seniority: mid-to-senior IC. Senior enough to define the test strategy independently; hands-on enough to build it. Real IC appetite. title: Senior Field Service Engineer
description: At Carbon, our mission goes beyond 3D printing. We are enabling creators everywhere to make what the world needs, right now. Our company is built on the idea that diverse fields of study must come together to solve intractable problems. We have grand ambitions to create technology that will influence industry around the world. You will be joining a diverse team with a vibrant culture, where team success is as important as celebrating individual contributions. Help us change the world and we will help you change yours. The support team works to ensure that customers love us and love our products. We are accountable for customers’ success and positive experience with Carbon3D. Field Service Engineers work with our Service and Engineering teams to address issues at customer sites. This role reports to the Field Service Engineering Manager. Location: This is a remote role with frequent travel, based out of a home office preferably in Michigan. We are looking for someone living commutable (driving) distance from Detroit Metropolitan Airport (DTW). This role is not eligible for current Visa sponsorship or transfer. Responsibilities: Frequent travel 75-90% to perform onsite equipment installs, maintenance, and upgrades Familiarizing customer of product usage and care Develop processes and documentation for standard service actions Recognize trends and patterns in field failures and feedback to the development team to drive future designs Work with engineering and manufacturing teams to ensure new issues are fully investigated and those countermeasures are in place Provide support to engineering and manufacturing teams as needed Availability for occasional off-hours calls and work Ability to travel Internationally Requirements: 5+ years of relevant experience BS in engineering field preferred but not required Must have hands-on approach Ability to read electrical schematic and mechanical drawings Excellent verbal and written communication skills Strong troubleshooting skills with mechanical/electrical systems Strong customer service experience required Personal car required Passport required You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Carbon, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills. At Carbon, we look at the person holistically and carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining salary. The compensation bracket for this position in Michigan is $82,800 - $124,200 (per year). In order to maintain equitable internal pay practices, we aim to hire new employees near the midpoint of $103,500, taking into account your experience, work location, certifications, and the unique skills you bring to the role. Carbon also offers to our eligible employees a comprehensive total rewards package that includes equity, benefits, and time off programs. For details on our total rewards package, visit https://www.carbon3d.com/about/life-at-carbon . #LI-Remote. #LI-MRWC By clicking the “APPLY NOW” button and submitting your job application, you agree you have reviewed the complete Privacy Notice for Employees, Independent Contractors and Job Applicants , which explains the categories of personal information we collect about you, the purposes for which the categories of personal information shall be used and your rights with respect to our use of such personal Information.
